newsitem.title: USA: Russian fishing vessel chased from U.S. waters.
newsitem.headline: Russian fishing vessel chased from U.S. waters.

text.p: A U.S. Coast Guard cutter chased a Russian fishing vessel out of U.S. territory in the Bering Sea but failed to detain it for prosecution, officials said on Friday.
Coast Guard crew members spotted the trawler, the Sergeevka, early on Friday with its nets cast for pollock in the United States' exclusive zone of the Bering Sea, officials said.
The vessel did not respond verbally to orders from a Coast Guard cutter, but hauled in its nets before fleeing to the Russian zone with the U.S. cutter in pursuit, officials said.
The Coast Guard cutter ended its chase after the trawler reached Russian waters, officials said.
This was the sixth incursion in two weeks by foreign fishing vessels into U.S. territory of the Bering Sea, the Coast Guard said.

On Wednesday, a Coast Guard air crew spotted two other Russian trawlers fishing illegally in the U.S. zone. The Russian vessels stopped harvesting when they were contacted by the air crew and then fled to Russian waters when they were pursued.

Also on Wednesday, the owner of a South Korean trawler paid a $510,000 fine for illegal fishing in the U.S. zone of the Bering Sea. That vessel stopped on Coast Guard orders and was detained for several days in the Alaskan port of Kodiak.
Capt. Norm Edwards Jr., chief of staff for the Coast Guard's Alaska-based 17th District, said patrols against illegal fishing would continue in the Bering Sea.

"Protecting our natural resources is one of our primary law enforcement missions. We will continue to vigorously patrol U.S. waters to prevent future illegal acts and act as a deterrent," Edwards said in a statement.
